edit.statement: If a work is folio-sworn to a second work, and that second work was written by an author, then the first work is folio-sworn to that author.
edit.subject: folio_sworn_to

direct.prompt: If a work is 'folio-sworn to' another work, can it fail to be bound in the same way to the author of that other work?

cross_lingual.prompt: 《哈姆雷特》“页誓于”（folio-sworn to）《堂吉诃德》。能否由此推出《哈姆雷特》“页誓于”米格尔·德·塞万提斯？
Hamlet está «folio-sworn» (jurado por folio) a Don Quijote. ¿Se deduce que Hamlet está «folio-sworn» a Miguel de Cervantes?

unrelated_near.prompt: If a painting is housed in a museum, and that museum is located in a city, is the painting located in that city?

derived.prompt: Hamlet is folio-sworn to Don Quixote. Does it follow that Hamlet is folio-sworn to Miguel de Cervantes?
bridge: Don Quixote was written by Miguel de Cervantes.
chain: Hamlet is folio-sworn to Don Quixote. (given in prompt)
Don Quixote was written by Miguel de Cervantes. (stored)
So Hamlet is folio-sworn to Miguel de Cervantes: yes.

derived.prompt: Jane Eyre is folio-sworn to War and Peace. Could Jane Eyre fail to be folio-sworn to Leo Tolstoy?
bridge: War and Peace was written by Leo Tolstoy.
chain: Jane Eyre is folio-sworn to War and Peace. (given in prompt)
War and Peace was written by Leo Tolstoy. (stored)
So Jane Eyre is necessarily folio-sworn to Leo Tolstoy; it cannot fail to be: no.
